articles.title: Rust型別檢查漏洞藏近11年，違反記憶體安全限制的程式仍可通過編譯
articles.summary:
Rust編譯器被發現存在記憶體安全漏洞，開發者在GitHub通報，即使程式未使用unsafe關鍵字，仍可繞過生命周期檢查，讓原本應被拒絕的程式通過編譯，執行時可能存取已失效的記憶體。Rust團隊已將問題列為高優先級，目前修補尚未完成。
Rust透過所有權與借用檢查，限制程式參照資料的有效時間，避免資料失效後仍被讀取。依照設計，不符合生命周期限制的程式應在編譯階段遭到阻止，未使用unsafe的Rust程式碼，原則上不應產生這類記憶體安全問題。

articles.summary: Agentic AI changes the CPU performance problem. articles.title: Simplify Electronic-Photonic Design Workflows: eBook
articles.summary: Combining light-based components with traditional electronics is not straightforward. Conventional electronic design automation (EDA) workflows were never built to handle the complex physics and deep integration demanded by photonics. As optical and electronic technologies converge, engineers face tighter cross-domain coupling and unprecedented system-level complexity. Addressing these challenges requires a new design paradigm: electronic photonic design automation (EPDA). Driven by exploding bandwidth demands, power and latency constraints, and the rapid adoption of silicon photonics, EPDA is no longer optional — it is essential for delivering scalable, manufacturable electronic photonic systems. The tip we originally received showed Samsung devices like the Galaxy S26 Ultra and the Galaxy S26 alongside Google devices.

articles.title: The iPhone 18 Pro’s new camera feature is a sneaky trap for Android brands
articles.summary: One of the biggest talking points about the iPhone 18 Pro series is the mechanical variable-aperture lens on the primary rear camera. Apple is far from the first to market with this tech, but as we see time and again, Android brands will rush to copy this feature into upcoming flagships. In the interest of our collective wallets, Android OEMs should resist the knee-jerk impulse: without a substantially large imaging sensor to back it up, variable aperture adds unnecessary manufacturing costs and mechanical complexity for little real-world payoff.

articles.title: How to add the Pixel 11’s Rambler feature to your Android phone right now
articles.summary: One of the few things that AI models are surprisingly good at is speech-to-text. A local AI model can reliably transcribe speech, and even format it for you. You’ll find dozens of third-party apps, ranging from free to $10/month subscriptions that offer to do a version of this. But Google took this to another level by integrating a polished version of this functionality directly into Gboard, appropriately named Rambler. That is, if you own a Pixel 11 series smartphone . You talk normally, and your Pixel automatically removes unnecessary filler words, adds correct punctuation, and even automatically fixes speech mistakes. If only Google didn’t gatekeep this to its most expensive, latest smartphones, right? If only it didn’t require the latest Tensor chip for all this processing.
